description: The chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets per year, separated by the number of languages represented in each dataset (monolingual versus multilingual). The horizontal axis contains the categorical time variable labeled “Year,” with years shown in chronological order from 2012 through 2022. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and is displayed on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels shown at approximately \(10^1\) and \(10^2\) (indicating tens and hundreds); bar heights span from roughly a few datasets up to a little over 100. Each year is represented by up to two adjacent bars, as indicated by the legend titled “Languages”: blue bars correspond to “1” language and orange bars correspond to “2+” languages. Approximate bar heights for the blue (1-language) series are about 2 in 2012, about 2 in 2013, about 3 in 2014, about 3 in 2015, about 12 in 2016, about 20 in 2017, about 45–50 in 2018, about 60–70 in 2019, about 100 in 2020, and about 140–150 in 2021; for 2022, the blue bar appears in a lighter shade and is around 30–35. The orange (2+ languages) series appears starting in 2017 at about 5, is about 2 in 2018, about 7 in 2019, about 20 in 2020, about 10 in 2021, and in 2022 an orange bar in a lighter shade is near about 2. Bars are grouped by year (side-by-side rather than stacked), and the 2022 bars are visually de-emphasized using paler shades compared with prior years.
